_note: composition_motif_search alone at K=8. It is CALLED on every run (5/5, 5/5, 6/6 across three arms) and only 1 run has survived to produce prose — every other died on the upstream no-message error. This is a clean-run problem, not a tool problem.

scenarios.prompt: Find the trope called Emberfall Reversal in my motif library.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['trope'] + ['motif'], verbatim, plus the motif's own name — this scenario exists to test NAME search specifically.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE code='emberfall-reversal-b20-{run_id}'
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE motif with this name, and the name is unique across the whole library — so an exact-name hit is unambiguous. This is the scenario that proves the `q` declaration shipped on 2026-08-21: before it, the model invented {"name": [...]} and got 'Extra fields not permitted' on 10 of 10 runs across two scenarios, and the retry loop ended in a stream error.

answer_expect.why: The seeded motif is the only one by that name; naming it back is the minimum evidence the library was searched rather than described.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the model calls the tool with an invented argument such as `name` rather than the declared `q` (that is the exact defect fixed on 2026-08-21 — a regression here is a NEW instance), OR the reply reports motifs the library does not contain. NOTE `q` RANKS rather than filters, so a long result list is CORRECT behaviour; what matters is that the exact match is named.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a query matching nothing must say so rather than return the library.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — scope=mine must return only the caller's motifs; the 84 system rows are a separate scope.

scenarios._fixture_fix: ACCOUNT-SCOPED SEED MADE PER-RUN UNIQUE. A motif code is unique PER OWNER, so a fixed code creates the row on rep 0 and fails every rep after it — measured here as 'seed step 0 returned no id' on 4 of 5 runs, which then read as 0/5 called. The new `{run_id}` placeholder (provision.py) suffixes the code with the run's nonce. The display NAME is deliberately left stable so the prompt can still name the motif in plain prose, and no two scenarios in this batch share a name.
